title: Generate a usable idea pool
instructions: Continue from this task contract: I will explain to secondary-school readers how one school-learned skill or idea applies in another area of life, using a specific actual or realistic example. Answer all six questions about generating usable ideas before choosing or ordering them.

parts.prompt: Which candidate most directly fits the task contract?

options.text: Schools should teach more subjects because education is important.
A science lesson taught me to compare evidence before deciding; I used that habit when my club compared two fundraising plans.
My favourite school day included sport, lunch and a class celebration.
Youth blogs should publish more colourful photographs.

choice_rationales.A: This broad opinion does not show one school-learned idea applied in a different area of life.
choice_rationales.B: This candidate names one learned habit, a different setting and a specific personal application.
choice_rationales.C: This is a school-day narrative rather than an explanation of transferred learning.
choice_rationales.D: This discusses blog design rather than the required practical lesson.

parts.hint: Check for one school-learned idea, a different life setting and a specific application.
parts.correct_explanation: Comparing evidence transfers from a science lesson to a specific club decision and therefore stays inside the task contract.

parts.prompt: A learner notices an older sibling use a study timetable to prepare for a sports tournament. Which idea source is the learner using?

options.text: Direct personal experience
Observation of another person
A dictionary definition
An unrelated opinion

choice_rationales.A: The learner observed the sibling rather than carrying out the action personally.
choice_rationales.B: The candidate comes from noticing another person's behaviour in a real setting.
choice_rationales.C: No word meaning is being looked up.
choice_rationales.D: The observation can supply relevant evidence when it is connected to the selected learning.

parts.hint: Ask who performed the action in the example.
parts.correct_explanation: Watching a sibling apply a timetable is an observation of another person.

parts.prompt: Which THREE details make the charity-sale idea developable with the I-S-A-R frame?

options.text: The school-learned idea is breaking a large problem into smaller parts.
The situation is planning a school charity sale.
The action is separating publicity, supplies, prices and staffing.
Problem-solving is useful for everyone everywhere.
The event was certainly the greatest success in the school's history.

choice_rationales.A: This identifies the transferable learning precisely.
choice_rationales.B: This provides a concrete setting outside the original mathematics problem.
choice_rationales.C: This gives observable actions that a paragraph can explain.
choice_rationales.D: This general claim adds no specific situation or action.
choice_rationales.E: This unsupported dramatic claim is unnecessary and may be fabricated.

parts.hint: Select the learning, situation and action; avoid a general slogan or unsupported success claim.
parts.correct_explanation: A usable frame identifies the learned method, places it in a concrete new situation and shows specific action.

parts.prompt: Which candidate should be rejected as off-task rather than merely needing more detail?

options.text: Using a history timeline to organise preparations for a family trip
Applying teamwork learned in a group project while helping at a community event
Explaining why the youth blog should change its logo and colour scheme
Using careful measurement from science when rearranging furniture in a small room

choice_rationales.A: This can fit the task once the action and result are developed.
choice_rationales.B: This transfers one learned skill to a different setting.
choice_rationales.C: The blog is only the writing situation; its visual design is outside the composition topic.
choice_rationales.D: This connects a school-learned practice to an everyday application.

parts.hint: Find the option that cannot answer the task contract even after adding detail.
parts.correct_explanation: Advice about the blog's visual design does not explain how school learning applies elsewhere in the writer's life.

parts.prompt: Which sentence uses a plausible future scenario honestly?

options.text: Last year I led a rescue operation, although this did not happen.
Everyone knows this method always guarantees success.
I could use the checklist method when organising our next class event so that equipment and deadlines are not missed.
Imagine something impressive and write it as a true memory.

choice_rationales.A: This presents an invented past event as fact.
choice_rationales.B: This makes an absolute claim without a concrete personal application.
choice_rationales.C: The phrase ‘could use’ signals a realistic future application and supplies a specific purpose.
choice_rationales.D: Invented experience should not be disguised as truth.

parts.hint: Look for language that clearly signals possibility rather than a false memory.
parts.correct_explanation: The sentence openly presents a credible future use and explains what the method would help the writer do.

parts.prompt: Which completed I-S-A-R frame is most usable for later paragraph planning?

options.text: Idea: teamwork. Situation: life. Action: work together. Result: good.

Idea: checking evidence. Situation: choosing between two club fundraising plans. Action: compare cost, likely participation and possible risks. Result: recommend the better-supported plan and explain the choice.
Idea: education. Situation: school. Action: learn. Result: become successful.
Idea: creativity. Situation: the best day ever. Action: something amazing. Result: everyone was impressed.

choice_rationales.A: The labels are present, but every entry is too vague to develop.
choice_rationales.B: The frame contains a precise learned habit, a bounded situation, concrete comparison actions and a credible result.
choice_rationales.C: The situation remains inside school and the entries are broad abstractions.
choice_rationales.D: The action is unspecified and the result is an unsupported dramatic claim.

parts.hint: Choose the frame that supplies enough concrete material to explain how and why the transfer works.
parts.correct_explanation: The evidence-checking frame is relevant, specific, honest and detailed enough to become a developed paragraph.
